QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_24

question.text: For an eligible start-up, when is the perquisite tax on ESOPs deferred to under the special provision?

answer.text: The perquisite tax is permanently exempt for start-up ESOPs
Deferred until 3 years from the date of exercise
Deferred to the earliest of: 5 years from allotment, date of sale of shares, or date of cessation of employment
Deferred until the date of sale of shares only

explanation.text: The Logic: For eligible start-ups, the Income-tax Act defers the perquisite tax on ESOPs (the FMV-on-exercise minus exercise-price spread). Under this deferment, the tax is payable at the EARLIEST of three trigger events: (1) expiry of five years from the date of allotment of the shares, (2) the date the employee sells the allotted shares, or (3) the date the employee ceases to be employed with the start-up. This deferment is designed to address the cash-flow mismatch where employees would otherwise owe tax on illiquid paper gains. The Trap: Option A wrongly suggests permanent exemption — the rule provides deferment, not exemption. Option B uses three years instead of the five-year clock. Option D captures only the sale-of-shares trigger and ignores the five-year and cessation-of-employment triggers, leaving employees exposed if they leave the start-up. Note: The cited workbook chapter (NISM Series-X-B_Investment Adviser Level 2.pdf, pp. 263-264) supports the deferment of TDS/tax payment for eligible-start-up ESOPs but does not explicitly enumerate the three trigger events (5 years from allotment, sale of shares, cessation of employment). The framing above is general Indian tax-law knowledge under the Income-tax Act.
